coreIdea: Ambiguous = two parse trees for one string. Left recursion breaks LL(1); ambiguity breaks ALL LR(k). SLR(1)⊊LALR(1)⊊LR(1).
mustRememberFormulas: Left recursion removal: A→Aα|β becomes A→βA', A'→αA'|ε
CNF derivation of length-n string: exactly 2n-1 steps
Ambiguous grammar ⟹ NOT LR(k) for any k
Operator grammar: no ε-productions, no adjacent non-terminals on RHS

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: 'remove left recursion' or 'eliminate ε-productions' or 'convert to CNF'
grammar given, asked what language/strings it generates
operator-grammar check, CFG-limitation question, or SDT value trace

commonTrapsQuickList: Left+right recursion together does NOT automatically imply ambiguous — verify directly
LL(1) ⟹ unambiguous, but unambiguous does NOT ⟹ LL(1)
Watch for INDIRECT left recursion (through another non-terminal), not just direct A→Aα
CFG cannot express context-sensitive constraints (declare-before-use) — needs semantic analysis beyond grammar
highYieldPyqLessons: Parser-class determination (12/47) and language-identification (12/47) are tied as the biggest sub-skills — together over half the topic.
This topic is the direct foundation for LR Parser and Syntax Directed Translation — get grammar classification fluent before moving on.
